ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB \perp AC$, $AB=AC$, $DE$ passes through point $A$, and $CD \perp DE$, $BE \perp DE$, with the feet of the perpendiculars being points $D$ and $E$, respectively, $CD=5$, $BE=3$. What is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because \angle CAB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAC+\angle BAE=90^\circ$,\\
$\because CD\perp DE, BE\perp DE$,\\
$\therefore \angle D=\angle E=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAC+\angle DCA=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAE=\angle DCA$,\\
$\because AB=AC$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ADC\cong \triangle BEA(AAS)$,\\
$\therefore AD=BE, CD=AE$,\\
$\because CD=5, BE=3$,\\
$\therefore AD=3, AE=5$,\\
$\therefore DE=\boxed{8}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the bottom side is a horizontal straight line segment, points D, A, E are on the same straight line, and A is located between D and E; point C is directly above D, and line segment CD is perpendicular to the bottom side DE; point B is directly above E, and line segment BE is perpendicular to the bottom side DE; line segments AC and AB both start from A and connect to C and B respectively, and CB is also drawn in the figure. Reasoning: Because AB ⟂ AC, ∠CAB=90°. Also because D, A, E are collinear, rays AD and AE are opposite directions of the same straight line, therefore ∠DAC and ∠BAE together form complementary angles related to ∠CAB, so ∠DAC+∠BAE=90°. In right triangle ADC, CD ⟂ DE and AD is on DE, so ∠ADC=90°, hence ∠DAC+∠DCA=90°. Comparing the two equations gives ∠BAE=∠DCA. Also BE ⟂ DE, so ∠BEA=90°, equal to ∠ADC. It is known that AB=AC, therefore triangle ADC and triangle BEA have one pair of equal right angles, one pair of equal acute angles, and corresponding sides AC=AB, and are congruent to each other. From congruence, AD=BE and AE=CD. It is known that BE=3, CD=5, so AD=3, AE=5. Because A is between D and E, DE=AD+AE=3+5=8.
